rationale: Le Curseur du Désordre is a strong, materially distinct addition to the catalogue. It explicitly stages the chance/order axis (P5) as a single draggable native range slider, with the slider literally being the axis — a clean P1 collapse of mechanism and concept. The Molnár reference is well-chosen and previously absent from the lineage, and the work answers A Chance of Order (2021) and Arranged According to the Laws of Chance (2026) by refusing to fix a single throw. The verdict text carries the idea with dry wit (P9), and the build is appropriately minimal (P3).
reservations: The novelty is real but the form (slider scales a random field over a grid) is a familiar generative-art gesture; the work leans heavily on the Molnár reference to do the conceptual heavy lifting. The 'live verdict' is a nice touch but the per-visit seed is held only in RAM, so reload resets the field — fine, but it means the 'same chance field' promise only holds within a single visit, which slightly weakens the P1 claim that the slider is the axis (the axis itself is re-seeded each visit).
revision_suggestion: Consider seeding the random field from a stable per-day or per-session key (e.g., today's date) so the axis is genuinely the same field across visits and the slider truly traverses one continuum rather than re-throwing it each load. Also consider a tiny attribution to Molnár's Interruptions more visibly in the surface (e.g., a single interrupted line at the 1% mark) to deepen the double-coding.
